12. First of all, issue no. (iv) is taken.
Issue no.(iv) is that whether the present suit is barred by Section 477 & 478 of the DMC Act?
Onus to prove this issue is upon the defendant no.4.
As per Section 477 of the DMC Act, no suit can be filed against a corporation or municipal authority for anything which has been done by authority in good faith.
As per Section 478 (1) of the DMC Act, there is a requirement of giving prior notice of two months before filing of any suit against the MCD.
However, as per Section 478 (3) of DMC Act, the condition of giving prior notice shall not apply to the suit in which only relief claimed is an injunction.
In the present suit, the relief claimed by the plaintiff against the defendant no.3/MCD is only the relief of injunction.
No any other relief is claimed by the plaintiff against defendant no.3/MCD.
Defendants have not placed on record any document/evidence to discharge their onus to prove that suit of the plaintiff comes under the purview of Section 477 & 478 of DMC Act.
Hence, issue no. (iv) is decided against defendants and in favour of plaintiff.

25.

In the present case, the plaintiff sought a mandatory injunction directing the defendants to remove the AC, AC ducts, water purifier systems, iron staircase, "etc." installed in the public lane of the property.
The inclusion of the term "etc." in the prayer clause is vague and non-specific.
It leaves room for interpretation and creates ambiguity about the extent of the relief being claimed.
The court cannot be expected to assume or presume what the plaintiff intends to include under the umbrella of "etc".

It is a well-established principle of law that the relief sought in a plaint must be specific, clear,
and unambiguous.
The purpose of this requirement is to ensure that the court can precisely understand what relief is being claimed and can adjudicate upon the specific grievances presented by the plaintiff.

26. During the pendency of the suit, the plaintiff filed a second application under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 CPC r/w Section 151 of CPC seeking the interim relief of removal of water tanks and the same was dismissed by the court.
The previous application under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 CPC which was filed along with the plaint was not pressed.
Despite seeking the interim relief of removal of water tanks, the plaintiff did not amend his plaint to specifically incorporate a prayer for the removal of these water tanks.
The court cannot grant a relief that has not been explicitly sought.
It is the plaintiff's responsibility to ensure that all grievances and reliefs are clearly articulated in the pleadings.
The omission to amend the plaint to include the prayer of removal of the water tanks is a significant lapse on the part of the plaintiff.
The court is not expected to assume or speculate on what the plaintiff might have intended to seek.
The plaintiff must expressly state the relief, and the court can only grant what is specifically sought.
As a result, the court cannot grant a mandatory injunction for the removal of water tanks that were never specifically prayed for.
27. Accordingly, in view of the above discussion, both the above said issues are decided against the plaintiff and in favour of defendants.
